title: Apollo Taps European Private Credit Markets With New Lending Platform
detail:
Apollo Taps European Private Credit Markets With New Lending Platform
Zacks Equity Research
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 12:12 PM EST 4 min read
APO
GS
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Apollo Global Management, Inc. APO is expanding its private credit business with the launch of European Credit Company ("ECC"), a dedicated European lending platform with more than €10 billion ($11.2 billion) in lending capacity. Backed by Apollo funds and institutional investors, the platform will focus on performing corporate and asset-backed credit, strengthening APO's European lending capabilities.

How Will ECC Strengthen APO's European Lending Business?

The launch comes as demand for alternative financing gains momentum across Europe. As companies increasingly look beyond traditional banks for funding, private credit has emerged as an important source of capital. Rising institutional demand and the relatively low penetration of nonbank lending offer further room for market growth, creating opportunities for Apollo to expand its lending activities.

To capitalize on this opportunity, Apollo is building ECC as a dedicated pan-European origination and financing platform. It will provide financing across multiple credit asset classes, including corporate and asset-backed lending. ECC will target large and mid-market financing opportunities involving companies, financial sponsors and real asset owners, particularly in sectors such as infrastructure and real estate. The platform currently operates across Frankfurt, Jersey, London, Luxembourg City and Milan, with plans to expand into additional European markets in the upcoming quarters.

Beyond its presence in these markets, ECC will leverage multiple channels to expand its lending business. These include proprietary loan origination, partnerships with European financial institutions and access to Apollo's existing European credit platform. By combining these channels, ECC could strengthen local relationships, reach a broader pool of borrowers and generate additional lending opportunities across the region.

The launch also complements APO's broader efforts to expand its global private credit business and strengthen institutional relationships. In October 2026, the company announced a strategic investment to acquire a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, a move expected to deepen its Middle East relationships and broaden access to global alternative investment opportunities. Earlier, in September 2024, it partnered with Citigroup C to establish a $25-billion private credit and direct lending program. These initiatives, alongside ECC's launch, support Apollo's efforts to expand lending capabilities, strengthen origination networks and capture opportunities across international credit markets.

title: Meta Reportedly Plans To Raise $20B From Its Cross-Border Bond Sales, Including Debut Euro Offering

Meta Reportedly Plans To Raise $20B From Its Cross-Border Bond Sales, Including Debut Euro Offering
Shashank Nayar

META
C
MS
EUR=X
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Meta Platforms Inc. is targeting at least $20 billion in a multi-currency investment-grade bond deal to gauge market appetite amid climbing skepticism over AI expenditures.

The company tapped Citigroup Inc. and Morgan Stanley to coordinate investor discussions for a transaction that will mark its first major debt issuance in six months and its maiden euro-denominated offering.

Maturity schedules for the potential issuance span five to 30 years for dollar-denominated notes and roughly four to 38 years for the euro tranche.

Meta Platforms (META) is exploring a substantial cross-border debt package of about $20 billion to fund its ongoing operations and capital needs, Bloomberg reported.

However, the report noted that final sizing has not been locked in and could expand based on active investor participation.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

To kick off the process, the social media titan enlisted financial institutions Citigroup (C) and Morgan Stanley (MS) to lead investor discussions. The upcoming move follows a non-deal European roadshow held by the company last month, setting the stage for its first major debt transaction since April and its inaugural entry into the European bond market.

Surging AI Spending

The aggressive capital raise comes amid a broader wave of heavy borrowing by major technology firms. Over the past year, tech giants have rushed to raise hundreds of billions of dollars to construct data centers and buy advanced semiconductors. However, this heavy spending cycle has triggered anxiety regarding long-term financial returns.

Market unease is increasingly visible, with the cost of protecting prominent US technology debt against default reaching new peaks. Meta's proposed structure features dollar-denominated maturities ranging from five to 30 years, alongside euro notes stretching from just over four years to nearly 38 years.

Investor appetite for technology credit has visibly cooled since April when Meta previously tapped the high-grade market for $25 billion amid heavy demand, forcing issuers to offer sweeter terms. Peers like Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL) and Oracle Corp.(ORCL) have recently had to offer elevated yields and new-issuance concessions to attract buyers for multi-billion-dollar deals.

Beyond debt markets, Meta has aggressively tapped equity channels to support its ambitious artificial intelligence roadmap. The company recently priced $25 billion in common stock, secured $12.5 billion through preferred shares, and outlined plans to pull in up to $60 billion via an at-the-market equity distribution program.

Can Lazard's Campbell Lutyens Buyout Drive Long-Term Growth?

Trading disclosure

Lazard, Inc. LAZ is strengthening its position in the rapidly evolving private capital advisory market as it seeks to diversify revenues and establish growth opportunities beyond traditional merger and acquisition (M&A) advisory. In sync with these efforts, the company acquired Campbell Lutyens and established Lazard CL, marking an important step toward expanding its capabilities across private markets.

How Will Campbell Lutyens Strengthen LAZ's Growth Prospects?

The acquisition significantly enhances Lazard's ability to serve institutional investors, private equity sponsors, and asset managers seeking capital formation and liquidity solutions. With more than 300 advisory professionals across 19 offices worldwide, Lazard CL benefits from an expanded global footprint and specialized expertise in private equity, private credit, infrastructure and real estate.

The combined platform provides access to approximately 4,000 institutional investors through a dedicated distribution team of more than 60 professionals. This extensive investor network should strengthen Lazard's ability to execute fundraising mandates, facilitate secondary transactions and connect clients with alternative sources of capital.

The acquisition brings together Lazard's existing private capital advisory operations and Campbell Lutyens' expertise in fundraising, secondary transactions and general partner (GP) capital advisory. The combined business operates as Lazard's third global business alongside Financial Advisory and Asset Management. Further, integrating private capital advisory with Lazard's M&A, restructuring and capital markets businesses is expected to create cross-selling opportunities, attract additional mandates and drive advisory fee growth.

Can Lazard CL Become Meaningful Revenue Contributor?

The financial implications of the transaction are encouraging. Management anticipates $500 million in combined Lazard CL revenues for 2027 and expects the acquisition to be accretive to earnings that year, even before considering potential revenue or expense synergies.

The addition of a substantially larger private capital advisory platform should create another avenue for fee generation. Although private capital revenues remain sensitive to transaction activity and fundraising conditions, expanded exposure to primary fundraising, secondary advisory and GP capital solutions could reduce Lazard's dependence on conventional M&A mandates.

The development also complements Lazard's improving operating momentum. In the third quarter of 2026, the company generated adjusted net revenues of $805 million, increasing 11% year over year. Its Financial Advisory business delivered record third-quarter revenues, reflecting the benefits of investments in talent and advisory capabilities.

Will Citigroup's Cost-Cut Initiatives Boost Long-Term Profitability?
Riya Anand

Trading disclosure

Citigroup Inc. C continues to streamline operations through workforce reductions, organizational restructuring, technology modernization and automation. These initiatives are expected to reduce operating complexity, generate productivity savings and support sustainable profitability.

As part of this transformation, the company announced its plan in January 2024 to reduce its global workforce by nearly 8% by 2026. It reduced headcount to 217,000 as of Sept. 30, 2026, from 227,000 a year earlier. The bank incurred more than $1 billion in severance expenses in the first nine months of 2026 to drive structural efficiencies. Workforce optimization, reduced management layers and technology investments are expected to generate $2-2.5 billion in annualized savings by 2026.

Beyond workforce optimization, Citigroup is driving efficiency through process simplification, platform consolidation and increased automation, reducing manual touchpoints across operations. At the same time, the company continues to invest in technology and artificial intelligence to strengthen operational resilience, improve productivity and support revenue growth. To accelerate these initiatives, Citigroup plans to invest an incremental $5 billion between 2026 and 2028, with spending focused on technology modernization, marketing, front-office talent and branch renovations.

C expects workforce optimization, organizational simplification and technology investments to generate $2-$2.5 billion in annualized cost savings by 2026. Management expects the full-year efficiency ratio to be slightly below 60%, improving to 55-60% in 2027-2028 and below 55% during 2029-2031. It anticipates return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) exceeding 11% in 2026, targeting 11-13% in 2027-2028 and 14-15% over the medium term.

Overall, Citigroup's restructuring and AI-driven productivity initiatives should support long-term profitability. Although elevated investments may constrain near-term gains, declining transformation expenses and recurring savings should strengthen operating margins.

Other Financial Firms' Cost-Cutting Initiatives

Navient Corporation NAVI is focused on reducing costs and improving operating efficiency to strengthen profitability. Navient's Phase 2 strategy, announced in November 2025, builds on Phase 1 initiatives introduced in January 2024, emphasizing cost reductions, operational efficiencies and improved capital efficiency at Earnest. Continued cost discipline and streamlining of its legacy portfolio are expected to support Navient's profitability.

Although rate hikes disappeared from the Federal Reserve's playbook for 3 years, Wall Street is preparing for another tightening cycle. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in 3 years, leaving the upper bound of the federal funds target range at 4.00%. Traders on Kalshi put a 72% market-implied probability on another 25-basis-point hike at the December 9 meeting. The core PCE price index, the Fed's preferred gauge, rose to 130.90 in its latest reading, the highest in a series that has climbed every month since November 2025. Why Rising Rates Fatten Bank Margins

For JPMorgan, Bank of America (NYSE:BAC), Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS) and Citigroup (NYSE:C), the key mechanism is net interest margin: the gap between what a bank earns on loans and securities and what it pays depositors. When the Fed hikes, floating-rate loans reprice higher quickly while many deposit rates lag behind, so the spread widens. That buffer shrinks when savers move cash into higher-paying CDs, when borrowers default, or when bonds bought at lower yields lose value. The pressure ran the other way in the zero-rate era, when 24/7 Wall St. reported that low rates forced banks to re-examine their strategies.

Investing.com -- Alstom shares fell over 6% in Paris after J.P. Morgan and Citi downgraded the rail company and cut their price targets following a profit warning that Citi said largely relates to a €5 billion backlog on the Coradia regional train platform.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

J.P. Morgan cut Alstom to "neutral" from "overweight" and lowered its December 2027 price target to €15.60 from €28, citing earnings cuts and a lower valuation multiple.

Citi moved to "neutral/high risk" from "buy" and cut its target to €14 from €28, saying the update "leaves as many questions as answers." It put the share price at €11.89 on Nov. 2, with a bull case of €25 and a bear case of €10.

Alstom took a hit of about €1 billion to adjusted EBIT in the first half, mainly on Coradia-Max projects, J.P. Morgan said. It called the size of the warning a surprise, given that Alstom took a hit of about €190 million in the second half last year.

Alstom guided for a free cash flow outflow of about €1.5 billion this year. J.P. Morgan expects free cash flow recovery to be delayed by at least 12 months because of ongoing execution issues, forecasting an outflow of €106 million in FY28 and an inflow of €918 million in FY29.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Citi expects limited free cash flow in FY28 because progress payments have shifted later and the Coradia carries higher costs and penalties.

J.P. Morgan forecasts an adjusted EBIT margin of 1.2% in FY27, while Citi forecasts 1.4%. Citi said margins could stay below 7% until the Coradia program is complete, as the six Coradia contracts are now loss-making, and that the earlier 8-10% target could be pushed out to at least FY31.

Citi cut its FY27 adjusted earnings forecast to €0.07 per share from €1.69, citing weaker near-term execution, and J.P. Morgan cut its forecast to a loss of €0.19 per share from €1.54.

Alstom announced a €2 billion deleveraging plan with organic and inorganic measures. J.P. Morgan said the plan is needed to maintain Alstom's investment-grade credit rating but will weigh on the share price in the coming months.

It said options could include asset or joint-venture sales, convertible bonds and a capital increase. Citi expects some equity capital raise.

J.P. Morgan said the backlog review will last until the end of the fiscal year and risks to second-half guidance cannot be ruled out, though it sees low risk of further provisions on the German Coradia-Max projects. Alstom is targeting to "normalize performance from the next fiscal year," while Citi said details of new mid-term targets are due in Q2'27.

What Wall Street Has Been Saying

Scotiabank raises its SoFi Technologies price target to US$26 and refers to Q3 as a record quarter with revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA, alongside improved credit and steady demand across borrow, spend, save and invest products.

Keefe Bruyette keeps an Underperform rating with a US$15 target and focuses on SoFi Technologies' use of fair value accounting. The firm highlights that higher rates and balance sheet growth can increase capital consumption and create headwinds when results are measured against guidance.
